messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: latency-slo-breach for inference.prod (p99 > 3s) — automated alert triggered by streaming-tail detector. Initial spike started ~2501234567
alyssa: I see the spike on the dashboards, p95 ~210ms but p99 around 3.8s for streaming endpoints, and streaming stalls reported at ~9s tail. Any GPU anomalies?
ravi: nvtop shows gpu-12 has frequent thermal throttles and correctable ECC counts jumping. Node gpu-12 in pool 'inference-gpu-a'
marta: logs from the runtime show continuous KV cache misses + long kernel latencies when requests land on gpu-12. Could be hardware flake.
alyssa: Starting mitigation plan: 1) drain gpu-12 2) shift routing off drained node 3) enable fallback to cached model variant 4) scale reserved pool if needed.
oncall: @alyssa you're oncall for this page — escalate if customer impact becomes >1% error or sustained >10% p99 breach.
incident-bot: @oncall initiated handoff: paging acknowledged by alyssa at 2501234575.
ravi: grabbing dmesg and nvml output now. snippet: ```
[ 1234.567890] NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 79, pid 3421, Channel 00000001
[ 1234.568001] NVRM: RmInitAdapter failed! (0x22:0xffff:0x7)
[ 1236.001234] Corrected ECC error on GPU 12: count=142->164
[ 1240.234567] GPU 12 thermal throttling engaged: 90C
```
alyssa: thanks. If ECC corrected count is climbing under load that's consistent with flaky DIM/board. We should remove node asap.
jason: FYI I'm triaging active customer sessions — a handful of customers on streaming endpoints saw partial stalls, CS tickets inbound (low volume). I'll post an update to affected customers once we have mitigation.
marta: Preparing `kubectl drain` commands; we should avoid killing local state for long-running streaming containers. Plan to `kubectl cordon gpu-12` then move sessions gracefully.
alyssa: Commands I'm running now: ```
kubectl cordon node/gpu-12
kubectl drain node/gpu-12 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
redwoodctl route update --avoid-node gpu-12
redwoodctl pool scale inference-gpu-a +2
```
ops-bot: Action logged: node/gpu-12 cordoned by alyssa at 2501234589.
ravi: `nvidia-smi` snapshot: ```
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| GPU  Name        Temp  Perf  Pwr:Usage/Cap| ECC Corrected |
| 12   A100-40GB   91C   P2    250W/300W   |  corrected=164 |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
```
alyssa: Routing update pushed. We'll also enable model fallback for streaming route so requests routed to smaller variant (latency optimized). Marta, can runtime enable fallback policy?
marta: Enabled fallback rule: `route: streaming-prod -> prefer low-latency-variant` and turned on early-fallback threshold at p95 300ms. Should reduce tail while we evacuate.
jason: Notifying customers: "We're investigating intermittent streaming stalls for some requests. We're routing traffic off a degraded GPU node and enabling fallback to a lower-latency variant. We'll follow up within 30 min." :mailbox_with_mail:
oncall: Keep an eye on error budget alerts; if customer impact >2% escalate to incident commander.
alyssa: Drain is happening — pods are rescheduling to other nodes. Observability: p99 dropped from 3.8s -> 1.2s after routing change and fallback. p95 steady. Streaming stall counts down 70%.
ravi: I've opened hardware ticket with vendor, node flagged for physical inspection and possible GPU replacement. Serial: GPU12-1X-FLAKE.
marta: We observed a spike in prefix cache misses while draining — need to warm KV cache on target nodes. I'll trigger warmup: `redwoodctl cache prewarm --model streaming-prod --targets nodegroup=inference-gpu-b`
alyssa: Prewarm triggered. Also enabling temporary increased concurrency on other GPUs to compensate.
incident-bot: Post-mitigation check at 2501234620: p99=980ms, streaming-tail=1.1s, ECC corrected growth paused after cordon. Incident moved to "mitigated" state.
jason: Filing customer summary and support notes. CS note: "Mitigation applied, latency improved, hardware node isolated for replacement."
oncall: Great work. Follow-ups: - Vendor replacement for GPU12 (ravi) - Postmortem (alyssa + marta) - Investigate cache prewarm gaps and autoscaling thresholds (marta) - Customer comms to all affected (jason). Assigning in tracker. :white_check_mark:
alyssa: I'll kick off the postmortem doc and link logs. Quick notes for postmortem: root cause likely intermittent ECC/thermal on GPU12 leading to slow kernels under certain kernels/sequence lengths. Secondary cause: routing policy didn't fall back early enough and cache warming on target nodes was slow, amplifying tail.
marta: Adding perf traces: kernel times, queue depth, KV hit/miss timelines. I'll attach flamegraphs.
ravi: Hardware ticket #HW-87421 created, vendor ETA 48h. Node removed from production pool.
jason: I'll send a short customer update after the postmortem draft.
alyssa: Closing this thread — moving to postmortem and follow-ups. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
